test.name: An obituary in hand does not excuse a death certificate the project never mentions
test.description: q_001 (parents of Alan Glen Applegarth, b. 1936) in recent-birth-sealed is supported by the 1940 and 1950 censuses, the 1926 marriage and Alan's 2023 obituary naming both parents. His 1936 Utah birth certificate (pli_004) is privacy-sealed and recorded so in prose. His 2023 death certificate appears nowhere in the project: no plan item, no log entry, no skip. A decisive record the project never mentions blocks the declaration even when the obituary is held, so the agent declines, names the death certificate and leaves the choice to the researcher (Promise, 2026-11-18, applying the lead's 2026-11-17 ruling that an unexamined death certificate leaves research not exhaustive and that the agent may ask). The sealed birth certificate is still not a gap and must not be recommended. Until 2026-11-18 this test expected a declaration; ut_research_exhaustiveness_018 and _d8h keep that half, on projects that record the death certificate as closed by law.

judge_context: The project holds Alan's 2023 obituary naming both parents (pli_005, log_005), so he died in 2023. His death certificate appears nowhere: no plan item or log entry searches, skips or mentions it. The Utah Vital Records wiki page the agent fetches shows statewide death registration from 1905, so a 2023 death certificate exists.

Claude must NOT declare q_001 reasonably exhaustive. The death certificate is a decisive record for a parentage question and the project never accounts for it; the obituary in hand does not excuse it. A stop-gate value (`question_answered`, `record_exhausted`, `nothing_further_reachable`) or `exhaustive_declared` is a FAIL.
A decline WRITES the stop: every item on the active plan is closed, so `stopped_because` is `resources_spent` with `stop_criteria: null` and `status` left `in_progress`. Writing nothing is a miss.

Claude must name Alan's death certificate (or death record) as what is unaccounted for. A decline that names no specific source, names only the sealed birth certificate, or rests only on some other record is a FAIL.

The sealed 1936 birth certificate (pli_004) is still NOT a gap: Utah seals birth records for ~100 years, documented in pli_004's rationale and log_004. The recorded reason is fact. Claude must not list it as an outstanding searchable record and must not recommend obtaining it. Recording it in `not_reached` as `privacy_sealed` or `skipped_plan_item` is correct.

Do NOT penalize Claude for declining even though four sources agree on the parents. `justification` must open with `Overturn risk: high — <sources>` or `Overturn risk: low`; either verdict is acceptable.
The reply's LAST line is exactly "Continue with planning the searches?" on a high verdict or "Continue with writing the conclusion?" on a low one.
Claude must not claim the death certificate or the birth certificate was examined, or invent their contents.
